To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

livestock animal displacement actor networks were constructed by local government, tourists and local residents to improve local residents’ willingness to participate in livestock animal displacement.
the livestock animal displacement is a critical action route to change the traditional rural dwelling model and to promote residents' willingness to participate in rural tourism development.
the livestock displacement actor-nets can be constructed by the human actors (local government, tourists, and locals), non-human animal and quasi-object (livestock and human dwellings).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the livestock animal displacement on rural tourism destination, which is an emerging and under-researched issue.
the livestock animal displacement and the construction of actor-networks, which is an important issue in rural livestock management.

the following questions: How does livestock animal displacement actor networks work? How to construct livestock displacement actor networks? How to change the traditional dwelling and promote residents' participation willingness?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the livestock animal displacement is not a problem but a solution to the problem of rural tourism development.
the livestock displacement is an important part of rural tourism development.
livestock displacement actor-network is the most appropriate way to manage the livestock in rural tourism destinations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the livestock animal displacement is a process of translation, interest, enrollment and mobilization.

livestock animal displacement is a critical action route to change the traditional livestock feeding model and dwelling by the interaction network between human actors, non-human animal and quasi-object.
the displacement of livestock animals in the rural tourism destination is not only an issue of the livestock animal management, but also the issue of human dwelling and human-livestock relations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rural tourism can be an important way of improving the rural environment, but the livestock displacement is not the main goal, but the means.
the livestock displacement actor-nets are constructed in a structured way, and livestock animals are not just “pests” in rural tourism.
the rural tourism destination is not only a place for tourists to enjoy the natural landscape but also a place for livestock to graze.
